barriers.reason: Patient cannot drive, is not steady enough to take the bus with a walker and transfer, and has no independent way to reach the hospital rehab center three times weekly.
The 9:00 AM Monday/Wednesday/Friday therapy times conflict with the daughter's 7-to-5 work schedule, which is the patient's only described ride source.

alternatives.text: Ask the rehab center for a later chair/appointment time or days that match when the daughter can take off or another ride is available.

If the patient has Medicaid or dual coverage, request Medicaid non-emergency medical transportation for standing rides to therapy; if Medicare-only, check whether the Medicare Advantage plan includes a transportation benefit rather than promising a covered ride.
Evaluate ADA Paratransit certification if the patient's condition prevents fixed-route bus use; note this is not immediate and runs only when fixed-route service operates.

barriers.reason: Patient is on a fixed income and already has unopened hospital/rehab bills, so ongoing apixaban, atorvastatin, and lisinopril costs may be unaffordable without assistance.

alternatives.text: Screen for Medicare Part D Extra Help/low-income subsidy or manufacturer assistance, and ask the prescriber about a lower-cost formulary equivalent if needed.
